name: NASA style
touchpoints: launch countdowns (the L-minus and T-minus clocks with built-in holds, the countdown clock at the press site), the launch director's GO/NO-GO poll, the front wall of mission control (a world map with the ground track, tracking-station circles and a row of clocks), the countdown block and fact cells on nasa.gov and the Earth Indicators charts

sample.topic: Launch readiness review of Vizney Space, a fictional launch provider, as of Nov 18, 2026 14:00 UTC: three upcoming flights (VS-12 crew rotation Nov 24 from launch site LS-1, VS-13 cargo resupply Dec 9 from LS-1, VS-14 Earth observation Dec 17 from LS-2 into a polar orbit), 14 to 16 positions in each GO/NO-GO poll, open items against a plan from L−45 to the L−2 review, 14 tracking stations, a catalog of 6,041 tracked objects below 1,400 km and each flight's close approaches in its first 72 hours. Launch sites and stations are named by number and region only; the orbit families copy the shape of low Earth orbit without naming any real system

canvas.role: page background, header and footer, the front-wall map and the code window (HDS carbon-black, the nasa.gov header and dark sections, measured)

card.role: every panel: figures, the table and the workbench sit on #17171b with square corners, no border and no shadow (HDS carbon-90, measured)

plot.role: chart background: the card itself, never a second panel

raise.role: tooltips (with a 2px white top rule), the hovered row, land on the front-wall map, the highlighted code line (HDS carbon-80)

rule.role: axis baselines, the dashed L−2 review marker, the diverging midpoint (HDS carbon-70)

divider.role: section, header and footer rules: white at 20% (the HDS rule on dark surfaces, rgba(255,255,255,.2), measured); inside the countdown band the same rule reads #3c64a7

ink.role: titles, values, clock digits, the subject line and the ground track in contact, the selected tab and its 2px underline, the focus ring (HDS spacesuit-white)

body.role: body text and table values (HDS carbon-10), 13.9:1 on the card

muted.role: subtitles, notes, keys, axis ticks and code comments (HDS carbon-40), 6.0:1 on the card

text-2.role: labels in DM Mono capitals and table heads (the HDS label), 6.0:1 on the card

dim.role: marks only, never text: the plan line, loss-of-signal dashes, open-item bars (HDS carbon-50, 3.7:1)

band.role: the countdown band behind the L− clock and the four key figures (the nasa.gov countdown block, nasa-blue shade, measured). White text 10.0:1; band labels and units white at 82% (#d3dceb, 7.3:1)

accent.role: nasa-red, UI only: the circle behind the arrow of a primary text button (Show more, the zip download). Never a data color

go.role: GO and good change as a mark (dot, bar); as text it is #4cd493

nogo.role: NO-GO: the status chip (black text, 5.8:1), the 3px rule on NO-GO rows, a station that is down (red dashes). As text it is #ff9088

validation.tool: dataviz validate_palette.js (OKLab), mode dark, on the card #17171b where every chart sits, run 2026-11-18
validation.categorical: blue #3d8af7, orange #d5691f and green #14a06a pass every check with --pairs all: lightness inside 0.48–0.67, chroma ≥ 0.1, worst CVD pair green↔orange ΔE 9.4 (deutan), worst normal-vision pair green↔blue ΔE 24.1, each ≥ 3:1 on the card. Other is carbon-60 #58585b
validation.status: GO #14a06a and NO-GO #f2473f: CVD ΔE 8.2 (deutan), normal vision 31.9, both ≥ 3:1. Status is always a word (GO, NO-GO) and NO-GO rows add a 3px rule, so color is never alone
validation.red-orange: NO-GO red and the orange category are only about ΔE 8 apart in normal vision, so red appears only for NO-GO and never in a figure that also uses orange
validation.subject: after the Earth Indicators charts the subject is white #ffffff (a 2px line, the ground track in contact) and the rest is gray: the plan #717173 with hollow #959599 rings each week, loss of signal #717173 dashed, gridlines #2e2e32
validation.sequential: one blue hue #1d52ad → #bcd6ff, dim to bright (on a dark card a larger value is brighter): monotone lightness, every step gap ≥ 0.06, hue spread 2°, the dim end 2.44:1 on the card
validation.diverging: blue arm #2b5aa6 → #98bdf5 (ahead, earlier; hue spread 1°, dim end 2.65:1) and orange arm #91491a → #f2a46d (behind, later; 6°, 2.70:1) each pass the ordinal checks; the midpoint is carbon-70 #444447
validation.text: label steps on the card: green #4cd493 9.5:1, red #ff9088 8.2:1, blue #7fb0ff 8.1:1, orange #f2a46d 8.8:1, gray #959599 6.0:1. On the countdown band: green 5.3:1, red 4.6:1, white at 82% 7.3:1
validation.scatter: the two scatters sit on black #000000 like the front wall: objects and passes are gray #717173 (4.4:1), the ones the title is about white #ffffff, and a pass over the maneuver line red #f2473f (5.8:1) inside a white ring; status always comes with the line names MANEUVER and WATCH and the 1 in N label

code.note: the screen's own text steps (blue keyword, green string, orange number, red function), all ≥ 7:1 on #000000

sans.role: body text, sentences, notes, keys and names in the poll and the table. Public Sans is the body face nasa.gov uses (SIL OFL)

display.role: the result sentence, figure titles, the business name, flight tabs and text buttons (nasa.gov headings are Inter 700 and 800, SIL OFL). Korean uses Pretendard

mono.role: the HDS label (500, small capitals with wide tracking), every clock and number (the L− clock and the four key figures at 300, call signs, L− dates, MET, table numbers, axis ticks) and code. Digits and call signs stay DM Mono in Korean; Korean labels drop the capitals and fall back to Pretendard

scale.headline: 27px/700 Inter (ko 25px), line-height 1.12, one sentence
scale.card-title: 19px/700 Inter (ko 17.5px), the finding as a sentence
scale.label: 11.2px/500 DM Mono capitals, letter-spacing .3125em (FIG 1 · GO/NO-GO POLL); ko 12px without capitals
scale.clock: 38px/300 DM Mono, tabular figures; units 13px/400 capitals at 82% white (DAYS · HRS · MINS)
scale.poll: 22px rows: call sign 12.5px/500 DM Mono, position name 13.5px Public Sans, dotted leader, status word DM Mono 500 (NO-GO on a red chip)
scale.note: 12.5px/400, the data source line under every figure

rows: header 60px, one line: business and report name, flight tabs (call sign in DM Mono and the kind; the selected one white with a 2px underline), EN/KO

first screen: the result in one sentence, then the countdown band (#0b3d91): flight, window and backup days, the as-of time; the L− clock (DAYS : HRS : MINS); four key figures in cells split by 1px rules, each label → value → change (poll GO count, open items against plan, weather % GO, margin to the L−2 review in days)
milestone strip under the band, 48px: the days from now to liftoff at one scale and the last 48 hours at a larger one, built-in holds as white blocks, L− labels, a NOW marker; below 640px a list

row 1 (584px | 1fr), bottoms aligned: Figure 1 GO/NO-GO poll (one row per position, NO-GO first with a 3px red rule, dotted leaders to the status word, need-by L− day, open-item bar and count) · Figure 2 mission control front wall (four clocks: liftoff UTC, % in contact, longest gap, events out of contact; a black map from 80°N to 70°S with the first three orbits, station circles at 5° elevation, a down station in red dashes, event diamonds; a contact timeline under the map)

01 Open items: Figure 3 open items against plan (white line, gray plan with hollow weekly rings, dotted pace to L−2, the title inside the plot in capitals) · Table 1 items to close (ID, item and type, position, need by, margin bar diverging from zero; six rows, then Show N more)

02 Orbit and traffic (1.22fr | 1fr), on the same black screen as the front wall: Figure 4 orbit map (every tracked object below 1,400 km as a dot by inclination and mean altitude, gray; the objects within ±25 km of the flight's first-week orbit white; the flight orbits as targets; a few orbit families named in place) · Figure 5 close approaches in the first 72 hours (four cells: passes, watch, maneuver, closest; MET by chance of collision on a log axis, a red dashed line at 1 in 10,000, a gray dotted line at 1 in 10 million, passes over the red line as red dots in a white ring with two-line labels)
03 How it's built · 04 Terms and counts · footer

motion.flip: 0.34s, the clock digits and key figures turn over 90ms apart
motion.grow: 0.5s, open-item bars grow from the left, 25ms apart
motion.draw: 1.4s, the open-items line and the ground track draw in, orbits 0.25s apart
motion.fade: 0.3s; the dots of Figures 4 and 5 fade in over 0.9s, the white band 0.45s later

tableau.fonts: Tableau Book for text; Inter, Public Sans and DM Mono only if installed on every viewing machine and the server

measured.date: 2026-11-18, Claude in Chrome (getComputedStyle in a same-origin 1440×900 frame): the nasa.gov home page, a mission page with its countdown block, and the science.nasa.gov Earth Indicators pages (carbon dioxide, global temperature) with their chart frames
measured.page: HDS (Horizon Design System) colors: carbon-black #000000, carbon-90 #17171b, 80 #2e2e32, 70 #444447, 60 #58585b, 50 #717173, 40 #959599, 30 #b9b9bb, 20 #d1d1d1, 10 #e3e3e3, 05 #f6f6f6, spacesuit-white #ffffff, nasa-red #f64137, nasa-blue #1c67e3 (shade #0b3d91), international orange #ea6f24, active green #47da84. Headings Inter 700 and 800, body Public Sans 400 16px, labels DM Mono 500 11.2px capitals with 3.5px tracking. Countdown block: #0b3d91, padding 16px 24px, digits DM Mono 300 28/32px, units DM Mono 400 11px capitals (DAYS · HRS · MINS · SECS). Fact cells: a 1px top rule, DM Mono label → Inter 700 value; rules on dark surfaces rgba(255,255,255,.2). Corners mostly square, round buttons 50%
measured.charts: Earth Indicators: the subject a 2px line, context gray 2px lines with hollow annual-mean circles, a 1px grid, ticks Public Sans 12.8px, the title in capitals inside the plot, a 'Data source: …' line below; ink and gray only
measured.notation: L-49H50M (L-minus, real time) and T-minus (stops during built-in holds), 'and counting', 'and holding'; GO and NO-GO; AOS, LOS and MET; countdown targets such as DEC 03, 2026, 11:59PM EST
measured.not_used: the NASA insignia, logotype, seal, mission patches and emblems, photos and imagery, the HDS icon set, real missions, vehicles, launch pads, centers and people

notice.en: Not an official NASA design, and not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by NASA. A reference style read from the publicly visible design of nasa.gov and science.nasa.gov and from public touchpoints such as launch countdowns and mission control displays; it carries no NASA insignia, logotype, seal, photo or data, and its fonts are open-licence fonts (SIL OFL). Trademarks belong to their owners.
